# 實質殖利率終於跟跌，晶片股卻再度重挫

## 債券反彈擴大，聯準會結果仍難預料

美債週二連續第三個交易日上漲，這次實質殖利率也參與其中。10年期殖利率下降4個基點至4.61%，包括實質殖利率降3個基點至2.41%，以及通膨補償降1個基點至2.20%。相較週一油價下跌只帶動損益兩平通膨率收窄、實質殖利率反升，反彈的基礎有所擴大。

美伊局勢降溫，減輕能源供應疑慮，布蘭特再跌1.62%至$86.93，延續2020年以來最差的三日表現。2年期與5年期美債殖利率各降5個基點至4.26%、4.35%，30年期降3個基點至5.09%。短端再度領漲，曲線略為轉陡，但交換市場仍給予隔日聯準會升息約三分之一的機率，決策前的不確定性明顯高於往常。

股市同樣分歧。S&P 500上漲0.21%，等權重指數創高，半導體卻下跌4.49%。中國技術進展與AI支出疑慮壓抑科技股，較低殖利率則有利債券基金。Meta資料中心融資的新細節，呈現這波投資潮需要付出的價格與契約保障；傳統併購融資則仍能以小得多的利差找到買方。

## 油價緩和拉低實質殖利率，政策路徑尚未明朗

短端領漲，使2s10s擴大1個基點至35個基點，2s30s擴大2個基點至83個基點，反轉週一部分牛市趨平。但一個月損失尚未抹平：2年期殖利率仍高19個基點，5年期與10年期高23個基點，30年期高22個基點。連漲三天後，長債殖利率仍在5%以上。

較有實質意義的改善來自抗通膨債。10年期實質殖利率2.41%，仍比一個月前高23個基點，但當日下降3個基點，已占名目殖利率跌幅大部分。前一日則是損益兩平通膨率下降5個基點，實質殖利率上升1個基點。週二不再只是市場降低通膨補償。

油價已回吐整週漲幅。布蘭特一週下跌4.48%，WTI收$82.24，一週跌3.14%；兩者一個月仍高約19%至21%。外交進展降低近期再度斷供風險，但能源尚未回到先前水準，企業依然面對較高燃料與運費成本。

紐約下午3時30分，交換市場估計週三升息25個基點機率約三分之一，完全計入9月前升息，至3月則接近50個基點。多數經濟學家預期維持利率，但Citadel Securities已把升息列為基本情境，PGIM也認為市場低估了這項風險。分歧不只在通膨，還在於主席Kevin Warsh是否會用未事先預告的決策，確立不同的溝通方式。

部位顯示，風險高度集中在這場會議。8月聯邦基金期貨未平倉量，從週五909,714口增至週一967,136口，超過2024年10月合約的紀錄。2026年較後月份SOFR選擇權也出現部位累積。即使現券反彈，美債期貨中防範長債下跌的保障，仍比押注上漲更昂貴。

Warsh已成立工作小組檢討溝通，並質疑反覆預告政策路徑的做法，交易員因此少了往常的確定感。2015年以來，決策前一天定價與最終結果的平均誤差僅2.4個基點；這次卻計入約8個基點緊縮。維持利率仍是較可能結果，但遠非投資人過去常見的近乎確定。

油價及實質殖利率下降，改善了債券眼前環境。週三將決定會議風險解除後，這些改善能保留多少；一個月殖利率仍偏高，加上長端避險成本昂貴，顯示投資人尚未放下對存續期間損失的擔憂。

## AI債利差低於發行，租約與殘值保障成焦點

依週二TRACE交易價格，Sopaipilla的Meta專案債利差約267個基點，低於發行時的287.5個基點。這筆約$125億交易在週一以約7.53%殖利率定價，銷售近一週，條件卻未從初步討論收窄。摩根大通策略師指出，最終利差為三年來A級以上債券最寬。$200億訂單僅1.6倍，今年投資級發行平均約4倍，借款人須付出明顯讓利。

新揭露的租約與資產保障，說明投資人以這個殖利率取得哪些權利。Meta將是德州1吉瓦園區初期唯一租戶，專案預計2028年營運、開發成本約$140億，BlackRock基金持有80%、Meta持有20%。租約先簽4年，附四次延長選擇權，潛在期間合計20年。若資料中心公允價值低於事先約定門檻，殘值保證在特定情況下補足差額，提供租約不續約或提前終止時的保障。

自2025年以來，全球AI相關債務已募集逾$5,700億，這些支持條件日益重要。保證讓專案更容易融資，卻不會消除經濟風險。Nvidia前一日CDS創紀錄升幅，已使市場注意逾$7,500億潛在基建安排，包括客戶融資與保證。週二中國浸潤式深紫外光微影技術的進展，又增加競爭疑慮：融資承諾擴大之際，投入資金建出的產能可能面對更弱定價能力。

Brady併購融資的結構則單純得多。公司為以$14億收購Honeywell生產力解決方案業務，私募$8億投資級債，年期5至10年。最大一筆$3億7年期券，定價為美債加125個基點，另有銀行聯貸的$10億定期貸款。成熟營運資產同時支持銀行及私募需求，利差遠低於AI專案。

Tullow Oil希望利用商品價格帶來的額外現金流，降低融資成本。4月公司延長約$12億債券，以$4.23億票據取代$4億Glencore貸款，並增加貨物預付款融資。重整後債券約102美分，4月一船原油實現價格達每桶$130，使公司開始探索2027年更便宜的借款。但若2027年9月30日前未簽署出售協議，提前到期條款將使還款提早六個月。現金流改善創造機會，再融資仍取決於執行，以及如今正在回落的油價。

無評等市政債市場中，QCF/I計畫發行約$6.1億、2046年及2057年到期債，收購Advantage Behavioral Health，行銷水準約同年期AAA債加300個基點。其中約$4.15億付給Clearview Capital與公司內部人士，另有$1億依績效支付。企業價值中，自有不動產只有$1,440萬，還款主要依賴預估營運現金流。類似結構待發行約$30億，使這筆交易的先例意義不只限於單一案件。

歐洲銀行資本債對複雜風險給出的補償反而很少。多幣別AT1指數利差降至紀錄低點211.3個基點，兩家銀行的特別股重設利差也創最低。Man Group認為，買方低估了延長、取消配息及本金損失風險。強勁需求與其他結構型債務需要明顯讓利的情況形成對照。

軟體業再融資則進一步考驗市場容量。Veritas支持的Gainwell討論替換近$57億債務，包括約$42億第一順位及$15億第二順位貸款。債券加貸款方案可延長優先到期年限，次順位風險則可能留給原有貸款人。2028年前軟體業槓桿貸款到期約$920億，結果不只反映新資金意願，也涉及既有債權人願意留下多少風險。

債券基金隨美債上漲，LQD漲0.30%、HYG漲0.19%、JNK漲0.16%，一個月仍各跌2.44%、0.51%、0.63%。各種結構都能找到資金，但從Brady的125個基點，到Sopaipilla發行時287.5個基點，資產、保證與價格的差異，比單一「風險偏好回升」更能說明市場。

## 海外曲線各受退休金改革、財政與流動性牽動

歐洲長端仍有轉陡傾向。歐元10s30s交換曲線連續第三個交易日轉陡，但仍僅約10個基點；2月衝突曾抹去先前約60%的變動。財政發債增加，荷蘭€1.6兆退休金制度又轉向確定提撥，投資人預期短天期較能表現。市場另計入ECB年底前升息42個基點，短端有政策風險，長端則面對退休金需求改變。

日本的稅制與匯率帶來不同方向壓力。報導指出，首相高市早苗可能要求官員準備把食品消費稅降至1%、為期兩年，引發財源與新增日本公債供給疑慮。日圓仍弱於163兌$1；市場預期日本銀行可能加快升息、抑制進口通膨，推升短端殖利率，使曲線趨平。

交換市場給予9月前升息約29%機率、10月前78%，半數受訪經濟學家仍預期12月。政策利率1%，低於官員討論的約2%中性水準。加快緊縮可支持匯率，卻提高短期借款成本；財政寬鬆則在曲線更遠處增加另一項供給負擔。

台灣顯示，低殖利率市場也能因本地條件迅速重新定價。20年期標售偏弱，加上市場預期未來一年至少升息12.5個基點一次，5年期殖利率跳升16個基點至1.82%，為2008年11月以來最高。流動性與本地利率預期，壓過了美債反彈方向。

美國收盤後，智利央行一致維持4.5%，為連續第五次不動。布蘭特週二盤中曾低於$85，前一週卻一度高於$100，使幾乎全數燃料仰賴進口的智利，通膨前景大幅擺動。6月通膨仍為4.3%、高於3%目標，投資、消費與就業指標又轉弱。央行選擇維持利率，未因油價下降就恢復降息。

稍後英國財政評估顯示，能源變便宜也不會立即恢復預算彈性。NIESR估計，本屆國會任期內，通膨與能源成本可能侵蝕£240億公共服務支出購買力，以及約£30億財政規則餘裕。該機構預估2026、2027年平均通膨均3.1%，高於IMF與OECD平均2.4%，接近英國央行3%中間情境。NIESR預期政策利率維持3.75%，市場則計入至少兩次升息至4.25%。依其評估，舉債填補支出缺口，將使原已不可持續的債務路徑進一步惡化。

部分英國買方已轉向海外。多資產基金增加整體債券配置，卻在12月至6月間，把英債占固定收益配置由25%降至15%，改增德國、日本、澳洲、紐西蘭及加拿大。這些資金規模小於專門英債基金，但高名目殖利率仍不足以抵銷通膨與國內政治的不確定性。

## 波斯灣發行穩健，哥倫比亞換債卻受質疑

阿聯酋借款人維持市場管道，同時承擔戰爭溢價。截至7月28日，主權及企業以美元、歐元發行$303億，較一年前高33%，比同期舊紀錄多$37億。近期交易包括RAK Bank的$6億、Burjeel的$5億，以及Ajman的$3億伊斯蘭債，多數超額認購並從初步指引收窄。主權美元債利差仍約美債加77個基點，高於戰前65個基點。

哥倫比亞債務管理則面對另一種挑戰。審計長質疑10月以COP43.4兆TES換成COP35.4兆新券的交易。這減少約COP8兆名目債務並延長年期，卻把原本約7.25%票息換成11.75%與12%，每年增加約COP3,165億利息支出。

財政部主張，若保留較低票息，就需要更深折價與更多名目發行。但案件轉交紀律調查，仍使未來換債增加法律與制度不確定性。2025年初級赤字已達GDP的3.5%，此時減輕再融資壓力的代價，是更高的未來利息，以及更少其他支出空間。

烏拉圭準備增發2035年到期本幣債及2037年美元債。整體新興市場貨幣大致持平，石油進口國受惠，商品出口國則失去部分額外收入。新興市場股市下跌3.7%，主要來自亞洲科技股，而非全面匯率衝擊。

EMB與長天期新興市場美元主權債指數各漲0.24%，受惠於美債殖利率下降。美元指數僅跌0.04%至101.43。外部環境改善，但阿聯酋的衝突利差、哥倫比亞的換債爭議，都顯示即使融資管道仍暢通，風險也各不相同。

## 大盤上漲，半導體卻再度重挫

S&P 500漲0.21%，等權重指數創高，VIX跌2.46%至18.21%。防禦及非科技股抵銷前AI領漲族群的又一波回落。殖利率下降與大盤韌性同時出現，並非投資人全面逃離風險資產。

Nasdaq 100下跌0.98%，半導體下跌4.49%，後者一週與一個月跌幅擴大至10.69%、16.42%。中國技術進展，加重市場對AI回報與相互連結融資的疑慮，亞洲晶片股也重挫。能源成本下降有利多數市場，壓力則集中在這個資本密集產業。

黃金期貨跌1.25%至$4,023.40，美元幾乎不動，債券基金上漲。布蘭特跌1.62%至$86.93，WTI跌0.45%至$82.24，有助解釋美債同時走強。能源與實質利率帶來債券喘息，並未伴隨廣泛避險需求急升。

## 聯準會之後，薪資與大型科技財報接棒

週三FOMC將解決眼前維持或升息的問題。升息25個基點，將驗證交換市場仍保留的風險；維持利率卻保留近期緊縮選項，對債市的支持也會小於更耐心的訊息。2年期殖利率、聯邦基金期貨及實質殖利率，將反映路徑如何修正。7月31日僱用成本指數接著提供能源降溫後的薪資壓力證據，油價再漲則會讓兩項判斷都更複雜。

Microsoft與Meta在7月29日公布財報，Apple與Amazon於7月30日接續。收入、資本承諾及保證，將幫助投資人判斷融資需求是否有足夠現金流支持。Sopaipilla週二約267個基點利差提供當前比較，Nvidia保障成本及後續訂單簿，則可觀察晶片回報疑慮是否擴及更大企業的資產負債表。

英國央行7月30日、日本銀行7月31日決策。英國指引須面對NIESR的3.75%基本情境，與市場朝4.25%定價的差距。日本任何早於12月升息的訊號，都須連同日圓解讀：偏鴿訊息可能使日圓再弱至165兌$1以外，引發干預疑慮；加快升息則可能推高短端殖利率。美國決策之後，兩國匯債反應仍會影響美債的相對吸引力。

overall_summary.headline: 實質殖利率終於跟跌，晶片股卻再度重挫
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美債連漲三個交易日，這次不只靠週一那樣的通膨補償收窄。10年期實質殖利率降3個基點至2.41%，通膨補償降1個基點至2.20%，短端領漲、曲線略轉陡。布蘭特跌1.62%至$86.93，但交換市場仍給予週三升息約三分之一機率，8月聯邦基金期貨未平倉量已達967,136口。

債券基金上漲、S&P 500等權重指數創高，晶片股卻跌4.49%。Sopaipilla利差約美債加267個基點，低於發行287.5個基點；新揭露的4年租約、延長選擇權與殘值保證，說明高殖利率背後的支持。相較之下，Brady的7年期併購券利差125個基點，呈現融資複雜度差異。

海外仍有各自壓力：歐洲退休金改革、日本稅制與匯率、台灣殖利率急升，以及英國財政變數。阿聯酋發行穩健，哥倫比亞換債則因未來利息成本受質疑。聯準會之後，薪資數據、大型科技財報與英日央行會議接續登場。
overall_summary.summary: 油價延續回落，10年期殖利率降4個基點至4.61%，主要來自實質殖利率下降。大盤與信用債走強，半導體卻跌4.49%，聯準會升息機率仍約三分之一。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Real yields join the Treasury rally as chip shares slide again

## A broader bond recovery meets an uncertain Fed decision

The Treasury rally reached a third session on Tuesday, this time with real yields participating. The 10-year yield fell 4 basis points to 4.61%, comprising a 3-basis-point decline in the real yield to 2.41% and a 1-basis-point fall in inflation compensation to 2.20%. That was a change from Monday, when cheaper oil lowered breakevens but real yields still rose.

Brent fell another 1.62% to $86.93, extending its worst three-day decline since 2020 as US-Iran de-escalation eased concern over energy supply. Two- and five-year Treasury yields each dropped 5 basis points, to 4.26% and 4.35%, while the 30-year fell 3 to 5.09%. The front end led again, modestly steepening the curve. Yet swaps still assigned roughly a one-in-three chance to a Fed increase the next day, leaving investors exposed to an unusually uncertain decision.

The equity market's split was just as marked. The S&P 500 rose 0.21% and its equal-weighted version reached a record, but semiconductors lost 4.49%. Chinese technological progress and concern over AI spending weighed on the sector even as lower yields helped broad credit funds. The latest details of Meta's data-center financing showed the price and contractual protection needed to fund that investment wave; elsewhere, conventional acquisition finance continued to find buyers at much smaller spreads.

## Oil relief lowers real yields without settling the policy path

The front-led rally widened 2s10s by 1 basis point to 35 and 2s30s by 2 to 83, reversing part of Monday's bull-flattening. It did not erase the month's losses. Two-year yields remained 19 basis points higher over a month, five- and ten-year yields 23 higher, and the 30-year 22 higher. The long bond was still above 5% after three days of gains.

Real yields supplied the day's more substantive improvement. At 2.41%, the ten-year real yield remained 23 basis points above its level a month earlier, but its 3-basis-point daily fall accounted for most of the nominal rally. The previous session had delivered a 5-basis-point breakeven decline alongside a 1-basis-point increase in real yields. Tuesday's move therefore extended beyond a reduction in measured inflation compensation.

Oil had now reversed its weekly increase. Brent was down 4.48% over the week and WTI, at $82.24, was down 3.14%. Both remained roughly 19%–21% higher over a month, leaving firms with higher fuel and freight costs despite the recent relief. Diplomacy reduced the immediate threat of another interruption without returning energy prices to their earlier levels.

At 3:30 p.m. New York time, swaps implied about a one-in-three probability of a quarter-point increase on Wednesday. They fully priced an increase by September and nearly 50 basis points by March. Most economists expected a hold, but Citadel Securities shifted its base case to a hike and PGIM also judged that risk underpriced. The disagreement concerned not only inflation, but whether Chairman Kevin Warsh would use an untelegraphed decision to establish a different approach to policy communication.

Positioning showed how concentrated the uncertainty had become. Open interest in August federal funds futures climbed from 909,714 contracts on Friday to 967,136 on Monday, surpassing the record associated with the October 2024 contract. Options positions were also building around later-2026 SOFR strikes. In Treasury futures, protection against a long-bond selloff remained more expensive than protection against gains, despite the rally in cash bonds.

Warsh had formed a task force to review communications and questioned the practice of repeatedly signaling the likely policy path. That left traders without their usual degree of reassurance. Since 2015, the average error between day-before pricing and the eventual decision had been only 2.4 basis points; this meeting carried roughly 8 basis points of expected tightening. A hold was still the favored outcome, but not the near-certainty investors had often traded around.

Lower oil and real yields improved the immediate setting for bonds. Wednesday would determine how much of that improvement survived the removal of event risk, with monthly yield increases and expensive long-end hedges showing that investors had not abandoned concern over duration losses.

## AI bonds trade inside launch levels, with protection in focus

Sopaipilla's Meta-linked bonds were quoted about 267 basis points over Treasuries in Tuesday TRACE pricing, inside the 287.5-basis-point launch spread. The roughly $12.5 billion deal had priced on Monday at about 7.53% after almost a week of syndication, without tightening from initial discussions. JPMorgan strategists called the final spread the widest for an A-rated or better bond in three years. A $20 billion orderbook, only 1.6 times the sale versus roughly four times for investment-grade offerings this year, had left the borrower paying a substantial concession.

Newly detailed lease and asset protections helped explain what buyers received for that yield. Meta will be the initial sole tenant of the 1-gigawatt Texas campus, expected to start operating in 2028 and cost about $14 billion. BlackRock funds own 80% and Meta 20%. The leases begin with a four-year term and four extension options, providing flexibility over a potential 20 years. A residual-value guarantee covers certain shortfalls between the data center's fair value and a pre-agreed threshold, offering protection if leases are not renewed or are terminated.

That support matters in a market absorbing more than $570 billion of global AI-related debt since 2025. Guarantees can make projects financeable without making the economic risk disappear. Nvidia's record CDS increase in the previous session had already drawn attention to more than $750 billion of potential infrastructure arrangements, including customer financing and guarantees. Tuesday's reports of Chinese progress in immersion deep-ultraviolet lithography added a competitive concern: funded capacity could face weaker pricing power just as its financing commitments grow.

Brady's acquisition funding offered a less complex comparison. It sold $800 million of privately placed investment-grade debt for its $1.4 billion purchase of Honeywell's productivity-solutions business. Maturities ranged from five to ten years; the largest, a $300 million seven-year tranche, priced 125 basis points over Treasuries. Brady also had a $1 billion term loan syndicated among lenders. Established operating assets supported both bank and private-placement demand at a fraction of the AI project spread.

Tullow Oil was seeking to use a commodity windfall to reduce its financing costs. It had extended roughly $1.2 billion of bonds in April, replaced a $400 million Glencore loan with $423 million of notes and added a cargo-prepayment facility. With reworked bonds near 102 cents and an April cargo realized at $130 a barrel, the company was exploring cheaper debt for 2027. A springing maturity still brought repayment forward by six months unless a sale agreement was signed by September 30, 2027. Stronger cash flow created an opening, but the refinancing depended on execution and oil prices that were now falling.

In the unrated municipal market, QCF/I planned about $610 million of bonds due in 2046 and 2057 to acquire Advantage Behavioral Health. Marketing levels were roughly 300 basis points above comparable AAA debt. About $415 million would go to Clearview Capital and company insiders, with another $100 million contingent on performance. Owned real estate accounted for only $14.4 million of the business's value, leaving repayment heavily dependent on projected operating cash flow. A roughly $3 billion pipeline of similar structures made the deal a precedent worth watching.

European bank capital was receiving much less compensation for its complexity. A multicurrency AT1 index reached a record-tight 211.3-basis-point spread, and two banks priced preferred securities at record-low reset spreads. Man Group argued that buyers were underestimating extension, coupon-cancellation and principal-loss risks. The strong appetite contrasted with the concessions demanded for other highly structured debt.

Software refinancing brought a further test of capacity. Veritas-backed Gainwell was discussing replacement of nearly $5.7 billion of debt, including about $4.2 billion of first-lien and $1.5 billion of second-lien loans. A bond-and-loan package could extend senior maturities while existing lenders retained the junior exposure. With roughly $92 billion of software leveraged loans maturing by 2028, the outcome would matter for both new-money appetite and the risk incumbent creditors were willing to keep.

Broad funds gained with Treasuries: LQD rose 0.30%, HYG 0.19% and JNK 0.16%. Monthly losses remained 2.44%, 0.51% and 0.63%, respectively. Funding was available across very different structures, but the range from Brady's 125-basis-point tranche to Sopaipilla's 287.5-basis-point launch showed why issuer assets, guarantees and price were more informative than a single risk-on label.

## Foreign curves reflect pension reform, fiscal plans and local liquidity

Europe's long curve retained a steepening bias. The euro 10s30s swap curve steepened for a third session but remained near 10 basis points after the February conflict erased about 60% of the earlier move. Investors expected shorter maturities to outperform over time as fiscal issuance increased and the Netherlands shifted its €1.6 trillion pension system toward defined contribution. Markets also priced 42 basis points of ECB increases by year-end, leaving both policy risk at the front and changing pension demand at the long end.

Japan faced opposing pressures from tax policy and the currency. Reports that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi could direct officials to prepare a two-year reduction in the food consumption tax to 1% raised questions about funding and additional JGB supply. The yen remained weaker than 163 per dollar. The curve had flattened as short yields rose on expectations that the BOJ might tighten faster to limit imported inflation.

Swaps assigned about a 29% probability of a BOJ increase by September and 78% by October, while half of surveyed economists still expected December. The policy rate was 1%, below officials' discussion of neutral near 2%. Faster tightening could support the currency but raise short borrowing costs; fiscal easing would add a separate supply burden farther out the curve.

Taiwan showed how quickly local conditions could reprice a low-yield market. Its five-year yield jumped 16 basis points to 1.82%, the highest since November 2008, following a weak 20-year sale and expectations of at least one 12.5-basis-point central-bank increase over the next year. Liquidity and local rate expectations outweighed the direction of the US rally.

After the US close, Chile unanimously held its policy rate at 4.5% for a fifth meeting. Brent had traded below $85 during Tuesday after exceeding $100 the prior week, whipsawing the outlook for an economy importing nearly all its fuel. June inflation was still 4.3% against a 3% target, while investment, consumption and employment indicators weakened. The bank kept rates unchanged rather than resuming easing as oil fell.

A later UK fiscal assessment showed why cheaper energy would not immediately restore budget flexibility. NIESR estimated that inflation and energy costs could erode £24 billion of public-service spending power during the parliamentary term and about £3 billion of fiscal-rule headroom. It forecast inflation averaging 3.1% in both 2026 and 2027, above the IMF and OECD's 2.4% average and close to the BOE's 3% middle scenario. NIESR expected Bank Rate to remain 3.75%; markets priced at least two increases to 4.25%. Borrowing to fill the spending gap would, in the institute's assessment, worsen an already unsustainable debt path.

Some UK buyers had already diversified away. Multi-asset funds increased bonds overall but cut gilts from 25% to 15% of their fixed-income allocations between December and June, adding Germany, Japan, Australia, New Zealand and Canada instead. This was a smaller pool than dedicated gilt funds, but high nominal UK yields had not been enough to offset uncertainty over inflation and domestic politics.

## Gulf issuance holds up as Colombia's debt exchange draws scrutiny

UAE borrowers retained access despite the war premium. Sovereigns and companies raised $30.3 billion in dollar and euro bonds through July 28, 33% above a year earlier and $3.7 billion above the previous record for the period. Recent deals included RAK Bank's $600 million, Burjeel's $500 million and a $300 million Ajman sukuk. Most were oversubscribed and tightened from initial guidance. Sovereign dollar bonds nevertheless traded about 77 basis points over Treasuries, wider than 65 before the war.

Colombia's debt management faced a different challenge. The comptroller questioned an October exchange of COP43.4 trillion of TES for COP35.4 trillion of new securities. It reduced nominal debt by about COP8 trillion and extended maturities, but replaced coupons around 7.25% with 11.75% and 12%, increasing annual interest expense by roughly COP316.5 billion.

The Finance Ministry argued that retaining lower coupons would have required deeper discounts and more nominal issuance. A referral for disciplinary review nevertheless added legal and institutional uncertainty to future exchanges. With a 2025 primary deficit of 3.5% of GDP, the trade-off mattered: less rollover pressure came with a larger future interest bill and less room for other spending.

Uruguay moved to reopen local-currency bonds due in 2035 and dollar bonds due in 2037. Across EM, currencies were roughly unchanged as oil importers benefited while commodity exporters lost part of their revenue windfall. A 3.7% fall in emerging-market equities was dominated by Asian technology rather than a broad currency shock.

EMB and a long-duration EM dollar sovereign index each gained 0.24%, helped by lower Treasury yields. The dollar index slipped only 0.04% to 101.43. The external backdrop improved, but UAE conflict spreads and the Colombian exchange dispute showed the different risks still attached to otherwise functioning financing channels.

## Broad stocks rise while semiconductors fall sharply

The S&P 500 gained 0.21%, its equal-weighted version reached a record, and VIX fell 2.46% to 18.21. Defensive and non-technology shares offset another retreat in former AI leaders. Lower yields thus accompanied broad equity resilience, not a general rush out of risk assets.

The Nasdaq 100 fell 0.98% and semiconductors 4.49%, taking the latter's weekly and monthly losses to 10.69% and 16.42%. Asian chip shares also suffered as Chinese capacity developments added to doubts over the returns on AI investment and interconnected financing. The pressure was concentrated in a capital-intensive sector even as most of the market benefited from lower energy costs.

Gold futures fell 1.25% to $4,023.40, the dollar was nearly unchanged and credit funds advanced. Brent's 1.62% decline to $86.93 and WTI's 0.45% fall to $82.24 helped explain the simultaneous Treasury gains. Bonds were receiving relief from energy and real rates without an accompanying surge in broad haven demand.

## The Fed decision gives way to wages and megacap results

Wednesday's FOMC will settle the immediate hold-or-hike question. A quarter-point increase would validate the risk still embedded in swaps; a hold that leaves near-term tightening open would offer less relief than a more patient message. Two-year yields, federal funds futures and real yields will show how investors revise the path. The July 31 Employment Cost Index then provides evidence on wage pressure after the energy impulse has eased. Renewed oil strength would complicate both assessments.

Microsoft and Meta report on July 29, followed by Apple and Amazon on July 30. Revenues, capital commitments and guarantees will help investors judge whether the financing pipeline is backed by adequate cash generation. Sopaipilla's Tuesday spread near 267 basis points offers a current reference, while Nvidia protection and subsequent orderbooks will indicate whether concern over chip returns is spreading into larger balance sheets.

The BOE decides on July 30 and BOJ on July 31. In Britain, guidance will confront the gap between NIESR's 3.75% baseline and market pricing toward 4.25%. In Japan, any suggestion of a hike before December must be read alongside the yen: a dovish message risks renewed weakness beyond 165 per dollar and intervention concern, while a quicker path could raise front-end yields. Their bond and currency responses will matter for the relative appeal of Treasuries after the US decision.
